q1_issues.issue: Mints an entity of the class `level`, a word the text never uses, to stand for the value "April's 6 percent".
Attaches a `Time` role to `sk_level_1`, which is an entity and not an eventuality, to render the possessive "April's".

`(Most high sk_level_2 unemployment_rate)` names `unemployment_rate` as the comparison class while the parse types `sk_level_2` as `level`, so the superlative's required `(Member X <class>)` companion is absent and the two atoms contradict each other.
"since July 1994", which restricts the span over which the new figure is the highest, is dropped entirely — no time atom anywhere records it.
The differential is on scale `rate` while the superlative is on scale `high`, so the size of the rise and the ordering it produced sit on two unrelated dimensions.

q2_gaps: A scalar-change "from X to Y" path whose endpoints are measured VALUES rather than places or entities — Source/Goal are given only for spatial/motion results, and there is no licensed way to reify a point on a scale as a referent.
A superlative whose comparison domain is restricted by a time span ("its highest since July 1994") — `Most` takes only a scale and a class, with no slot for the span.
The magnitude of a CHANGE ("inched up one-tenth of a percentage point") — `MoreBy` is defined for the gap between two entities on a scale, not for how much one entity moved.
notes: The core clause is right — `unemployment_rate` witness with a noun-modifier genus only, the phrasal verb `inch_up` kept whole with no genus, `Patient` for the non-volitional change-of-state subject, `Past`. Everything concerning the two numeric endpoints is improvised.
